resources.string: NineGrid keeps your Magic: The Gathering collection and decks on your phone. Scan a binder page of nine cards, paste a list or search a card, and see what everything is worth.
Off. Choose a folder (for example Google Drive) to turn it on.

Everything is stored on this phone. A backup file lets you move to a new phone or recover from a mistake. It holds your cards, decks and deck rules, history, wishlist, boosters, friends, change log and settings. Not included: the AI key, the offline card database and the images.
NineGrid needs the camera to read your cards. Photos are not stored or sent.

Prices come from Scryfall: Cardmarket in euros or TCGplayer in dollars, normally the trend price, never the lowest price. Foils use the foil price. Scryfall gives one price per print: language and condition do not count, so a Japanese or played card shows the same price as an English near-mint one. Proxies count as zero. Prices are updated every day on Wi-Fi.

How to get the file: from your own Sheet in Google Sheets via File → Download → Microsoft Excel (.xlsx), or in the Google Sheets app via ⋮ → Share and export → Save as → Excel. Your collection lives on your phone: viewing and changing it works without internet too. Scanning and looking up cards needs internet, unless you download the offline card database. Make a backup now and then, or turn on the weekly automatic backup.
The offline card database holds all Magic cards (about 110,000). With it you scan and look up cards without internet, and imports are much faster. Prices keep coming with the daily update.

For each colour: how much of the mana symbols in your costs it takes, against how many of your lands can make it. If the lands lag more than 10 points behind, you will often miss that colour.
Commander brackets count two-card combos that can win or lock the game. Commander Spellbook decides which combos count. With such combos a deck is at least bracket 3, often 4.
No two-card combos: no influence on the bracket

Number of non-land cards per mana value. The verdict depends on the deck type (aggro, midrange or control). The land advice uses Frank Karsten\'s formula: based on the average mana value and cheap ramp, give or take one land.

Cards lying loose in your collection that fit this deck: the right colours, within your bracket and your own rules. They help with roles your deck is still short on, or with your theme. With Swap the card moves from your collection into the deck, and you choose what goes out.
Lands from your collection that make two or more colours of this deck. With Swap the land goes into the deck, and a basic land in a matching colour goes back to your collection.

Cards in this deck that contribute the least. They fill no role and don\'t fit the theme, cost 6 or more mana, go above your bracket or aren\'t a creature of your tribe. With Swap you choose what comes in instead, and this card goes back to your collection.
